findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: Chicken in the walk-in cooler was observed to be missing a date mark. Facility has increased their date marking in other locations. These items not date marked were date marked during the inspection.
Ensure that any food or drink items that are opened are recorded with the date they are prepped or open. This date of prep or opening is day one. On day seven, these food/drink items are to be discarded. For example, if something is prepped or opened on Sunday, then Saturday is Day 7 and the item shall be discarded at this time.
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

(G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: Facility was observed to have little flies around the bar area. To control their population, a general/deep cleaning of the bar area is required. Facility should speak with pest control services to obtain an enzymatic cleaner that is effective to pour down the bar drains to eradicate the issue.
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: A kitchen knife was observed to be stored between a cutting board and the metal wall of the prep cooler. This knife was removed from service and placed in the dish area for a wash, rinse, sanitize cycle. Ensure the storage of in use utensils is accomplished in a manner that prevents contamination of the utensil.
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: Peroxide cleaner is being used at the facility with no test strips available. Facility PIC is going to speak with EcoLab and obtain test strips for the peroxide sanitizer being used in the facility. Ensure appropriate test strips are used with the designated sanitizers in use.
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: The shelving units above the sauce station were observed to have visible residue and soil. Ensure the boxes are removed from the shelving and that the shelves are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of soil residue and dust accumulation.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
5-205.15: The ice container at the bar area is missing the drain pipe leading to the floor drain. This is causing water to be present under the ice bin and providing a potential water source for any pests. Ensure that a drain pipe is attached by a licensed plumber according to the Plumbing Code. 
5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; P and (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
5-205.15: The hand sink by the fryers has a constant drip. Ensure this is repaired according to the plumbing code by a licensed plumber.
5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; P and (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-303.11: A lightbulb in the hood system was observed to be burnt out. Ensure this bulb is replaced to allow adequate lighting for the cooking area.
6-303.11: The light intensity shall be at least a certain lux and present in certain areas.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: The soda dispenser nozzles behind the bar were observed to be moldy and have accumulated filth over time. These nozzles were removed during inspection and will be properly washed, rinsed, and sanitized before use. Ensure these items are cleaned to prevent mold from accumulating.
4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.18: A bag of shredded lettuce was observed in the walk-in cooler past the expiration date. This bag was discarded during the inspection. Ensure date marking is accomplished and the best by dates are being followed to ensure the integrity of the food.
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
5-205.15: The hand sink by the fryers has a constant drip. Ensure this is repaired according to the plumbing code by a licensed plumber.
5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; P and (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: Caulking was observed to be needing repair in the following locations: Bar triple sink, sink with sprayer along cook line. These repairs need to be made by making the surface smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable while not allowing liquids or other various from accumulating in the gap between the metal and the wall. 
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16: Mops were observed in the mop basin to be stored in a manner that prevents air drying. These mops were placed in an upright position during inspection to allow proper air drying. Ensure this practice continues in order to keep the integrity of the mop heads.
6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment: REPEAT #1: Observed handwashing sink for bar to have spoon inside sink. Ensure handwashing sinks are for handwashing only. Corrected. Education provided. Handwashing sinks will be for handwashing only. Reference 5-205.11.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment: Observed chicken being cold held in a container. Chicken was measured to be 48F from probe thermometer. PIC stated chicken had been placed in container around 12. Corrected. Chicken was discarded. Education provided regarding cold holding and the benefit of maintaining logs at all times. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment: No proof of Certified Food Manager at the time of the inspection. Derrick is the person in charge and can show in the BWW system that his training expires in 8/2020 but the actual certificate with certificate number is not available. Robert McReynolds arrived during the inspection, but a CFM must be on site during all operating hours.
findings.citation_text: 750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment: Hand washing sink in the bar area was completely blocked with a cutting board. This sink did not have paper towels available either. Cutting board was moved and paper towels were provided to correct the violation.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11  (Pf) Hand washing sink blocked. Hand washing sinks must be accessible at all times. Reference 5-205.11.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment: Plastic cups are not being air dried after cleaning and sanitizing as cups are observed stacked with water in between. Wash, rinse, sanitize and air dry all dishes.
findings.citation_text: 4-901.11  (C) Equipment/Utensils are not properly Air-Dried after cleaning and sanitizing. After cleaning and sanitizing all equipment and utensils shall be air dried before use. Reference 4-901.11.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment: Handle to the chicken walk in cooler is missing the cover and therfore not smooth and easily cleanable. Replace the cover on this handle to avoid unnecessary crevices.
findings.citation_text: 4-101.19  (C) Nonfood-contact surfaces of are no longer easily cleanable. Repair handle with an corrosion-resistant, nonabsorbent and smooth material meeting National Sanitation Foundation/ANSI certification for use within a foodservice facility.  Reference 4-101.19.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be soiled: 1) the sides of the fryer and the reach in freezer next to the fryer with food debris accumulation, 2) the inside of the dish machine with limescale accumulation, 3) the drain cup for the soda gun at the bar with black debris accumulation, 4) the cabinets and plastic mats in the cabinets where the cups are stored in the wait stations along the Patio wall are soiled black underneath the mats. Clean these non-food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment: REPEAT> 1) Hand washing sinks in the kitchen are slow draining. 2) Dish machine is dripping water from the front of the machine when running. NEW> 3) The faucet at the three compartment sink appears to have a drip when off. Repair plumbing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15  (C) The plumbing needs repair. Repair plumbing according to Illinois and local plumbing code.  Reference 5-205.15.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment: Observed blue cheese dressing in the pump dispenser in the prep cooler to be probed at an internal temperature of 68F. This was congruent with the thermometer inside the bottom of the unit also. There were also numerous bags of this dressing in the produce walk in cooler that were probed from 53-60F. These bags may possibly have been stored in the bottom of the prep cooler before being placed in the walk in--these dressings were all discarded at the time of the inspection. Burgers and pico in the walk in cooler were probed at 40-43F. The service technician was called to address these cooler issues. Do not use the prep cooler until it is operating and able to maintain dressings at 41F or below at all times.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was discarded. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment: REPEAT> 1) Hand washing sinks in the kitchen are slow draining. 2) Dish machine is dripping water from the front right corner at the bottom of the machine when running. 3) Faucet on the left in the women's restroom is dripping when off. Repair plumbing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15  (C) The plumbing needs repair. Repair according to Illinois and local plumbing code.  Reference 5-205.15.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Sanitizer bucket on the cook line near the cold prep coolers tested at 100 ppm quaternary ammonium solution. This was time marked that it was prepared at 10:30am. Bucket was re-made during the inspection to provide 400 ppm quaternary ammonium as dispensed from the wall mounted unit at the three compartment sink. 4-501.114  (P)  Maintain concentration at 200 ppm to 400 ppm as indicated on manufacturer's label. Reference 4-501.114.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment: Observed the ice bin in the server area nearest the front door to be stored in the open position with no one around. Keep ice bin closed when not in use. Ice bin was closed during the visit.
findings.citation_text: 3-307.11  (C) Food shall be protected from contamination. Reference 3-307.11.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment: Observed employee stocking clean cups in the server stations, however, clean cups were stacked and water and moisture was observed between cups and employee was handling cups with bare hands that were in contact with the rim where customers may put their mouths. Proper air drying and handling of clean cups was discussed, and cups were taken back to dish to be run again. 4-901.11  (C)  After cleaning and sanitizing all equipment and utensils shall be air dried before use. Reference 4-901.11.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment: No proof of certified food manager at the time of the inspection. Provide a certified food manager certificate for the person in charge during each shift.
findings.citation_text: 750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment: Observed cups being stacked wet and placed in the cabinet in the waitress station near the door to the patio. Air dry all dishes before being stored.
findings.citation_text: 4-901.11  (C) Equipment/Utensils are not properly Air-Dried after cleaning and sanitizing. After cleaning and sanitizing all equipment and utensils shall be air dried before use. Reference 4-901.11.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment: 1) Observed the dish machine to be dripping water out of the from right corner at the bottom of the machine when running. 2) Observed the faucet on the left in the women's restroom to be dripping when off. 3) Observed the hand washing sinks throughout the facility to be slow draining and to accumulate water when washing hands. 5-205.15  (C) Repair according to Illinois and local plumbing code.  Reference 5-205.15.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed a gap in the baffles in the ventilation hood above the fryers. Manager reports that a new baffle is on order. Replace baffle.
750-700 Ventilation hoods shall be designed for easy cleaning and designed to prevent the cross contamination of food and food-contact surfaces by dripping grease or condensation.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed house made cajun aioli and pre-portioned corn to be date marked 7/22 and 7/19, 22, and 24 respectively. These were voluntarily discarded during the inspection. Date mark all ready to eat, potentially hazardous foods and hold no longer than 7 days maximum.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed an employee drink stored on a shelf in the kitchen with single service items and over gloves. Beverage was moved. Store beverages in designated areas on the shelves above the hand washing sinks at either end of the kitchen.
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed ice bins in the waitress station and at the bar to be stored in the open position when not in use. Store ice bins closed in between use.
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Observed a small cup being used as a scoop and stored in the coleslaw in the cold drawer. Dispensing tools should have a handle and the handle must be stored extended up and out of the food.
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
Dish machine in bar tested at 0 ppm chlorine. Apparently there was a kink in the line and lines were supposed to be replaced but there has been some change in service person for the dish machine company. Make sure these lines get replaced so that dish machine tests at 50 ppm chlorine each time. Machine was primed and line unkinked to get machine to test accurately during the inspection.
750-830 All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water disposed properly
findings.comment:
Observed the floor drain next to the walk in cooler (nearest the entrance) to be backed up and pooling water out onto the floor. See General Comments for more information. This needs to be repaired and plumbing looked at to ensure this always drains appropriately.
750-1050 All water containing sewage shall be disposed of  properly either by a public sewage system or an approved private disposal system which is constructed and operated in conformance with applicable State and local laws, ordinances and regulations.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.comment:
Observed a small gap between the bottom of the front doors and a gap between the doors leading to the Patio area. Seal doors to prevent rodent entry.
750-1170 Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: Observed 2 flats of chocolate milk and 1 flat of white milk to be probed at an internal temperature of 49F. These were sitting outside the beer walk in cooler as employee was rearranging coolers. Milk was discarded.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment: No paper towels at hand sink near fryers. Provide paper towels at each hand sink.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
Dish machine at the bar was testing at 0 ppm chlorine. Sanitizer bottle was nearly empty and was replaced during the inspection. Machine was primed and re-run to test at 50 ppm chlorine. Make sure staff is checking sanitizer concentrations at least daily to ensure dish machine at bar is always testing at 50 ppm chlorine.
750-830 All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
There is a drain just outside of the chicken walk in cooler at the end of the cook line, specifically where the fryers are that is not draining appropriately. Staff reports that drain intermittently does not drain well when the weather is cold and it sounds as though the grease from cleaning the floor may be coagulating in the drain when cold. Tom's Plumbing was consulted during the inspection and will be out this afternoon to address this issue. Maintain plumbing so that drains drain effectively.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed what appeared to be mold on the soda guns at the bar. Wash, rinse, and sanitize food contact surfaces.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
Observed no soap at the left hand side hand washing sink. Soap was provided to immediately CORRECT the violation.
750-1120e A supply of soap and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed a missing baffle on the left hand side of the hood. Replace baffle.
750-700 Ventilation hoods shall be designed for easy cleaning and designed to prevent the cross contamination of food and food-contact surfaces by dripping grease or condensation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed what appeared to be mold on the soda gun holders. Soda gun holders were removed and cleaned during inspection to immediately correct the violation.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
1) The seal along the main three compartment sink was separating from the wall. Reseal sink to the wall. 2) The seal along the bar three compartment sink was separating from the wall. Reseal sink to the wall. 3) The seal at the dump sink along the wait station was separating from the wall. Reseal sink to the wall.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.
